solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Capital, dude, a nuisance

parts.note: bud is American slang for a pal, as dude is
a pest is an annoying person or thing

explanation.surface: Someone addresses a mate and complains about an irritating city.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungary's seat of government, so it is an example of a national capital city.

clue.text: Rogue shackled by queen, perhaps, scold

indicators.note: the rogue is held inside the queen word, as if in chains

parts.note: a queen is one kind of bee
a rat is a scoundrel or rogue

explanation.surface: A villain in irons before the monarch is given a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen, perhaps' is not royalty but the queen bee.
explanation.definitionFit: To berate is to tell someone off angrily, the same as to scold.

clue.text: Like to consume French wine for sport

indicators.note: the first word consumes the second, taking it inside

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
vin is the French word for wine

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys drinking French wine as a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunging into water from a board is an Olympic sport.

clue.text: Authorise what to do with straight hair for a change?

definitions.meaning: to authorise is to allow or license

definitions.text: what to do with straight hair for a change?

explanation.surface: A hairdresser approves a new curly style for a client.
explanation.definitionFit: To authorise is to grant leave or allow something; the second reading splits the word as an instruction.

clue.text: Colleague heading for breakdown in no-win situation?

indicators.note: the single letter goes in the middle of the deadlock word

parts.note: a stalemate is a deadlock where nobody can win

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A co-worker is on course for a nervous collapse in a hopeless position.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a horse from the same yard, now any fellow member of the same team or firm.

clue.text: Plugging sink, secure instrument

indicators.note: one piece plugging another sits inside it, filling the gap like a stopper

parts.note: to set is to sink, as the sun does at dusk
to pin something is to fasten or secure it

explanation.surface: Someone stops up a basin and fastens down a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A small harpsichord-like keyboard, so a type of musical instrument.

clue.text: Pocket billiards team about to make a splash, perhaps?

definitions.text: about to make a splash, perhaps?

parts.note: pool is the American name for pocket billiards
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A pool team is about to make a big impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at the edge of a swimming bath is ready to jump in, which the clue jokingly describes.

clue.text: Hooker I bed in baseball team?

indicators.note: the I and the bed go in the middle of the team word

parts.note: a baseball team has nine players, so is called a nine
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A sex worker boasts of seducing a whole baseball team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooker' is not a prostitute but something that hooks you: an addictive drug.
explanation.definitionFit: The addictive chemical in tobacco gets smokers hooked, so it is jokingly a hooker.

clue.text: After shuffling round both poles, start to really move

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the poles, enclosing them
the letters of after are shuffled into a new order

parts.note: N and S stand for the north and south poles

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An expedition that has gone round both poles really starts moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a time word opening the sentence, but it is the fodder for 'shuffling'; 'both poles' means north and south.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfer something is to shift or move it from one place to another.

clue.text: Several switches on back of dimmer switch

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another comes after it
the back of a word is its final letter, here of dimmer
the letters of the word several switch places among themselves

explanation.surface: Lots of light switches are fitted to the rear of a dimmer control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Several' looks like a quantity but is the fodder for 'switches'; 'on' in an across clue puts that rearrangement after the dimmer's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch is a turnaround or change of position, which is what a reversal means.

clue.text: You've been caught cold in Batman's home, for the most part

indicators.note: the cold letter goes in the middle of the shortened city name
most of the word is kept, its last letter being dropped

parts.note: Gotham City is where Batman lives
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A taunt to someone caught out in the chilly city where Batman lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial exclamation said on catching someone out, meaning I have got you.

clue.text: Solid piece of furniture no good, one breaking

indicators.note: these letters break into the furniture word, splitting it apart

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sturdy item of furniture is useless because one part has broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Something solid is real and able to be touched, which is the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Already in transit, I sail westward

indicators.note: westward says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A traveller says they are already on the move, sailing west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the letters sitting inside 'transit, I sail'; 'westward' in an across clue means right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the present state of things, already, without change.

clue.text: Canine drinking last of water, one glass for cream

indicators.note: the tooth word drinks in, swallows, the letter

parts.note: a canine tooth is a fang

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a pane is a sheet of glass

explanation.surface: A dog laps up the end of its water, then a glass of cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' looks like a dog but is the tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: An almond-flavoured custard or cream used as a filling in tarts and pastries.

clue.text: Cheek concealing Republican indiscretion

indicators.note: the first word hides the second inside itself

parts.note: cheek is impertinence, impudence

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark hides a Republican politician's indiscreet behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiscretion is rash, unwise conduct, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Somewhat clever boxing match

indicators.note: the first word boxes in, encloses, the second

parts.note: sly means cunning or clever
a match gives a light; to light is to set a match to

explanation.surface: A boxing bout is rather smart.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to a small degree, a little.

clue.text: Vessel holding — and in — the drink?

definitions.text: Vessel holding — and in — the drink?

parts.words: Vessel holding — and in — the drink?
parts.note: the word names a tall glass holding beer or sherry, and also a sailing ship, which is in the drink, the sea

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a container that both holds a drink and sits in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drink' is slang for the sea; in Britain the word is also a large sherry glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a two-masted sailing ship and a large glass for sherry or beer bear this name.

clue.text: Stand out, as decay in moralist

indicators.note: the decay word goes in the middle of the moralist word

parts.note: a prude is a priggish moralist
rot is decay

explanation.surface: Corruption within a puritan really stands out.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick out from a surface, which is literally to stand out.

clue.text: Score onto delicate material for cutting

indicators.note: in an across answer, a piece put onto another follows it

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
a rating is a score or mark awarded

explanation.surface: Scoring marks onto fine fabric so that it can be cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacerating means tearing or slashing, so cutting is a close synonym, literally or of harsh words.

clue.text: Reversible dog collar put away

indicators.note: the pieces are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a pug is a breed of dog
to collar or nab someone is to arrest them

explanation.surface: A dog collar that can be worn either way is tidied into a drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: BANG UP is British slang for locking someone in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone away is to jail them, the slang sense of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Refuse all babies

definitions.meaning: a whole brood born to one animal at a time

explanation.surface: Someone declines to take every infant.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both scattered rubbish and the set of young born together to an animal.

clue.text: Not showing head, badger below street lit at night

indicators.note: in a down answer, the piece below another comes after it
the first letter of the word is not shown

parts.note: to harry someone is to badger or pester them

explanation.surface: A badger beneath a street lamp shows up at night without its head visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badger' is the verb, to pester, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear night sky full of visible stars is lit up by them.

clue.text: Not entirely unpleasant, old cave

indicators.note: not all of the word is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: grotty is British slang for unpleasant or shabby

explanation.surface: An old cave turns out to be not wholly unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: GROTTY is everyday British slang for grim or shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small cave, often picturesque, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Epic film about a criminal lover

indicators.note: the two words go around the a, enclosing it

parts.note: big means epic, grand in scale
a mist is a thin film, as on glass

explanation.surface: A blockbuster film is about a lover who breaks the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who marries again while still married commits a crime, so is a lawbreaking spouse.

clue.text: Go with tune composed for organ

indicators.note: the letters are composed, put together in a new order, as music is

explanation.surface: A musician is told to play along with a piece written for the church organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The muscular organ in the mouth used for taste and speech.

clue.text: Hood gets adjusted before beginning of race after horse going backwards

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the horse piece
the rearranged letters come before the start of race
the horse word is read in reverse

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

indicators.note: the letters of gets are adjusted, reordered
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: At the races, a hood is adjusted before the off on a horse heading the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' turns GETS into GSTE; 'going backwards' turns NAG into GAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hood is short for hoodlum, a violent criminal, so a gangster.

clue.text: Delivery from royal house, Tudor or Windsor?

parts.note: the House of York was an English royal dynasty
ER, Elizabeth Regina, fits Elizabeth I, a Tudor, and Elizabeth II, a Windsor

explanation.surface: A question about whether a parcel came from one royal dynasty or another.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a yorker is a ball pitched right at the batter's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket term for a kind of ball bowled, and each ball bowled is called a delivery.

clue.text: Ample bottles needed promptly, primarily for ladies' event

indicators.note: the first word bottles up, holds inside, the picked letters

parts.note: a hearty meal is an ample one

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letters of the words

explanation.surface: Lots of bottles must arrive on time for a women's celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-wedding celebration for the bride and her female friends.
